model_implication.initial_beb_scenario: The 18-BEB subtraction is contradicted by the December approximate 275+5 split. Retain as stress only; use five BEB plus about 275 trolleys as the 2023 central inventory if no better register is obtained.
model_implication.depot_implication: Nominal capacity alone does not prove feasibility: 2023 sources state all depots were full, while 2025 active fleet is below the 2020 nominal total. Mixed-class tracks, charging equipment and operational buffers are required.
model_implication.power_implication: The 78 MW result is system-wide planning evidence, not site firm capacity. A 2033 accelerated case needs earlier site scheduling than the 2040 roadmap.

central.grant_scope: Incremental route-conversion capital only. Common trolley replacement is excluded because the same electric renewal is required in the ordinary-renewal comparator.
central.grant_extension_note: grant_cases_with_common_trolley_capital applies a common-trolley grant only to the plan and is retained only as an intentionally asymmetric policy counterfactual. The symmetric_common_trolley case applies the same percentage to both comparator and plan.

boundaries: Vehicle and infrastructure leaves are CPI-rebased to constant 2023 CAD before aggregation; fixed FX and supply premiums remain explicit assumptions, not local bids.
Shared heavy-bus depot investment is sized from 1406 heavy positions and retained once. Class-specific charger/site items are added separately, but site power and civil works may still overlap.
The double-deck annual distance is a weekday-share proxy; the shuttle distance is an independently published 2023 actual total.

The approximate 275-trolley/5-BEB split comes from same-day public statements. Only 262 known trolley replacements occur; 13 existing electric assets are carried through 2033. If those also require renewal, purchases rise by 13.
Shuttle and double-deck manufacturing inventories include battery factors; the shuttle glider mass is not invented.
Depot construction and end-of-life are excluded from the environmental boundary.

The financial envelope excludes post-2023 battery replacement, retained pre-2024 asset terminal values, disposal proceeds and infrastructure terminal value; opposing omissions mean this is not a conservative bound or complete TCO.

london.source: TfL Bus Fleet Audit, 31 March 2023, detailed registration/body tables
london.plan_interpretation: One like-body electric bus replaces each non-electric fleet slot; existing electric slots due under the selected life cap are renewed. This is an order-batch plan at body-class level, not a route or garage plan.
residual_limits: Route-to-vehicle assignments and the required spare fleet are not in the audit.
Depot charging capacity, site power, delivery lead times and local prices are absent.
Life caps are sensitivity scenarios, not asserted TfL retirement rules.
The 2024 catch-up must be paired with facility-ready garages before it is operationally executable.

warnings: Emission factors are not a 2023 Vancouver chassis/PEMS certification.
CNG service km is inferred from purchased-gas energy and an EEA energy-consumption factor.
The gasoline-shuttle factor is the BC legacy inventory bus factor; no newer BC bus factor was located.
The high PM and NOx diesel/hybrid values are a conservative legacy-fleet envelope from the BC inventory, not a claim about every 2023 bus.
PM exhaust is treated as having PM2.5 = PM10 = TSP in the EEA workbook; the BC legacy rows retain separate PM2.5 and PM10 columns.
The existing transition scenario's 88.79 million non-deck fossil-km estimate excludes double-deck blocks and is a cross-check, not this audit's total activity denominator.
The five or so 2023 in-service battery-electric buses are not separately observable in the service-km feed; treating all non-trolley activity as fossil is a small conservative bias.
